event: Nala reads her Status through again, slowly, in wonder.
prose: You go back to the top and read it all again, slowly, line by line. A Status. Your Status, with a Class and Attributes and Paths, sitting in your mind in plain words.

event: She wonders what a Path is, and what Soulstealing and Exceptionalism will ask of her.
prose: What is a Path? A road you walk, or something that walks you? Soulstealing sounds like what you just did to the demon. Exceptionalism sounds like homework you already aced. You turn the words over and get nothing back from them.

event: The wonder wears thin; in the warm dark there is nothing to do but wait.
prose: After a while the words stop feeling new. The dark is warm and the heartbeat keeps time, and you can't see, or move much, or go anywhere. You are bored.

event: To pass the time she counts in her head: one, two, three, on and on.
prose: So you count. One, two, three, four. Past fifty, past a hundred, on into the hundreds, one number after the next.

event: Nala sets herself the Fibonacci exercise: modulo by n+2 down, every starting pair, every loop.
prose: You set yourself an exercise: Fibonacci sequences taken modulo n+2, then n+1, then on down, every starting pair carried round to its loop and to the length of that loop.

event: She works one modulus whole: every starting pair, every loop reachable, each loop's length.
prose: You start with n+2 and work it whole. Take a pair of numbers, add them, keep the remainder, carry the pair along, then the next, until a pair comes back that you have already had. That is a loop, and you learn it by its length. Then the next pair, until every pair under n+2 is held in memory with its loop.

event: She recites every result from the moduli before, then steps down to the next one.
prose: Before you take up n+1, you go back through what you have built: every pair under n+2, its loop, its length, recited once in order. Then you step down.

event: She keeps at it: run the pair, follow it round, name the loop, hold the length.
prose: Take a pair, follow it round until it closes, name the loop, hold the length, then take the next pair. Then the next modulus, and the same again.

event: Her reckoning slows and blurs, and she sleeps.
prose: The numbers start to slip. A pair goes missing from your hold, then another, and the loops run together in the dark. Somewhere in the middle of a modulus, you sleep.

event: She wakes in the dark at half past three, and goes back to her tables.
prose: You wake, and the dark is the same dark. You take up the tables where you left them, at the pair you lost.

event: The moduli come easier now; the loops fall into their places in her memory.
prose: The moduli come easier this time. A pair that took a long holding to run now closes quickly, and its loop sits where it belongs among the others.
